newsitem.title: INDIA: South Asian nations push ahead on closer trade ties.
newsitem.headline: South Asian nations push ahead on closer trade ties.

text.p: South Asian foreign ministers on Friday agreed to launch immediately a fresh round of trade negotiations on tariff concessions and to speed up measures towards free trade in the region.

Foreign ministers from seven South Asian nations at the end of two days of discussions called for "immediate launching of the third round of trade negotiations under South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA)", an official statement said.

SAARC comprises the Himalayan kingdoms of Bhutan and Nepal, the Indian Ocean island republics of Maldives and Sri Lanka, mostly Hindu India and its Moslem majority neighbours, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
Many of the region's 1.2 billion people live in dire poverty and would benefit from economic growth spurred by increased trade.
SAARC took the first steps towards forming a trade bloc last year with the creation of SAPTA, vowing to form a free trade zone by the year 2005.

Last month, SAARC member countries agreed to reduce tariffs on more than 1,500 products, up from 226 items covered in the first round of talks ended one year ago. But some 4,500 products remain untouched.
India, the most populous member state, has offered about half of the trade concessions and has been pressing for a third round of talks to accelerate the free trade movement.

The statement said the ministerial meeting asked the newly established inter-governmental expert group to prepare an early action plan to establish a South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), preferably by the year 2000.
Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told reporters the two-day meeting had been "very cooperative, very helpful and very friendly".
He said the last ministerial meeting had empahsised that political will was necessary for realisation of SAFTA.
"The actions undertaken subsequently is convincing evidence that all countries are committed to moving forward," Gujral said.
He said the foreign ministers had informally discussed sub-regional economic cooperation between Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal and India and Maldives, Sri Lanka and India.
"In forthcoming months we will activate this," he said.
Gujral told a questioner that there was no intention to isolate Pakistan from sub-regional cooperation.
"There is neither any intention nor any wish to isolate anybody, especially Pakistan (while forming sub regional groups)", he said.
Gujral said India would welcome any such cooperation whenever Pakistan so decided.
Uneasy ties between India and Pakistan have overshadowed SAARC's efforts for a free trade bloc.
India has failed to win most favoured nation (MFN) trade status from arch-rival Pakistan.

India has already granted MFN status -- under which two countries undertake to give each other the maximum tariff concessions on their mutual trade which they already grant to other countries -- to all SAARC nations, including Pakistan.
